item.title: Israeli army figures reveal sharp rise in Jewish attacks across occupied West Bank
item.description:
Israeli army figures reveal sharp rise in Jewish attacks across occupied West Bank

Submitted by Nadav Rapaport on Sat, 11/28/2026 - 11:02
Military data shows a 78 percent rise in 'Jewish nationalist crimes' compared with 2024, as rights group says settlers enjoy impunity for attacks
Israeli settlers watch Palestinian farmers picking olives in the village of Turmus Ayya, northeast of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, on 21 October 2026 (Zain Jaafar/AFP)
Off

Israeli settlers have committed at least 1,200 crimes against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank this year, killing seven and injuring 260 more, according to official Israeli military data.

Israeli news website Ynet reported that "Jewish nationalist crimes" in the Palestinian territory saw a 78 percent rise when compared with 2024, when Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz took office.

In 2024, settlers committed 675 attacks, killing six Palestinians and injuring 149 more.

In 2025, the number of attacks and casualties rose sharply, with the Israeli army recording 845 attacks that killed four Palestinians and injured 200 others.

In total, Israeli settlers have committed 2,720 "Jewish nationalist crimes" against Palestinians in the West Bank since the start of 2024, killing 17 Palestinians and injuring 609 more.

The report said that shortly after Katz took over the powerful ministry, he ordered the Israeli military to stop placing Israeli Jewish citizens in administrative detention, greatly limiting the ability of Israeli forces to arrest settlers.

This draconian measure, under which Israel can hold a person in detention for months without trial, is now reserved only for Palestinians, thousands of whom are currently held in Israel's detention facilities.

'The settlers are in control': How the West Bank is being ethnically cleansed
Read More »

According to a military official who spoke with Israel's Channel 12 News this week, the settler militias, known in Israel as the Hilltop Youth, are organised groups consisting of thousands of armed settlers. 

Ynet's report said that the Israeli army, the police and the Shin Bet are failing to protect Palestinians in the occupied territory from the settler militias, with the military official accusing the Shin Bet of avoiding gathering intelligence on upcoming settler attacks.

Shin Bet officials are committed to Israel's security, the official told Ynet, but "the problem there isn't the people, but the orders. It looks like they're not really in the picture," he said, implying that the agency's leadership is at fault for not addressing the mounting settler attacks.

Last year, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appointed David Zini, a settler from the occupied Syrian Golan Heights with close ties to the settler movement, to head the Shin Bet, raising concerns that Zini's far-right views would influence the agency's operations.

However, while the security official who spoke with Ynet mostly blamed the Shin Bet for the rise in Jewish nationalist crimes, the Israeli military is closely intertwined with the settler attacks, as soldiers protect the attackers and at other times even take part in the attacks.

Settler hotspots 

According to the Israeli human rights group B'Tselem, between the start of Israel's genocidal onslaught on the Gaza Strip in October 2023 and June 2026, the Israeli army killed 1,087 Palestinians in the West Bank.

By comparison, in the 23 years between 2000 and 2023, Israel killed 2,657 people in the area.

In September, the Israeli group said that Israeli soldiers, police officers and settlers enjoy "broad impunity" for the crimes they commit against Palestinians. 

‘My land is forbidden to me’: Israel’s settlement push encircles Jenin
Read More »

Between 2016 and 2024, the group said, 2,427 complaints were filed against soldiers for suspected crimes against Palestinians.

Investigations were opened in only 22.7 percent and indictments were filed in less than one percent of cases.

The rise in army and settler attacks against Palestinians overlaps with the appointment of another settler to a top Israeli security position, as since July 2024, Avi Bluth, a settler, has been heading the military's West Bank command.

Since his appointment, Bluth has led an extremely violent approach towards Palestinians, which includes razing entire refugee camps and relaxing the army's open-fire policy, while also advancing the establishment of settlements in the area.

According to Ynet's report, most Jewish nationalist crimes in 2026 took place in areas north of Jerusalem, with the Nablus Governorate suffering more than 34 percent of the crimes recorded by the army.

The governorate is the heart of a settlement resurgence in the area, as the Israeli far-right government, in the past four years, led a campaign to seize Palestinian land and establish settlements in the area. 

Other parts north of Jerusalem, such as the governorates of Ramallah, Tulkarm and Jenin, suffered together more than 33 percent of this year's crimes, while the area around East Jerusalem and the West Bank's southern parts of the territory, which include the governorates of Bethlehem and Hebron, suffered 30 percent of the attacks.

The rest of the Jewish nationalist crimes were committed in the eastern part of the territory, in the Jordan Valley, where the Israeli army and the settlers expelled Palestinian communities from their land over the past years.

item.title: Iran official: Iraq must not become a 'tool' of Trump
item.description:
Iran official: Iraq must not become a 'tool' of Trump

Mohammad Mokhber, an ​adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, warned Iraq in a post on X on Saturday that it must not become a "tool of Trump" after media reports that Iraq had closed several crossings following US efforts to blockade Iran's land borders.

“This unbreakable bond [with Iran] requires Baghdad to remain vigilant on the issue of borders so that it does not become a tool of the enemies of Islam or give in to the policies of the criminal Trump,” Mokhber said.

item.title: Pezeshkian announces return of damaged South Pars gas pipelines to production
item.description:
Pezeshkian announces return of damaged South Pars gas pipelines to production

Iran has repaired three gas pipelines damaged in the early weeks of the US-Israeli war, returning them to production at the South Pars gas field, the country’s state-run Mehr news agency said.

The agency said that lines 1 and 4 of the fourth refinery and line 3 of the sixth refinery were back in operation, adding 20 million cubic metres of gas a day to Iran's gas output capacity.

President Masoud Pezeshkian announced the development, saying: “Getting through the winter without cutting off electricity, gas, and fuel needed for production requires the support of the people, the efforts of producers, and improving infrastructure.”

War damage to Iran’s energy infrastructure has compounded energy shortages. As winter draws close, authorities have announced two-hour electricity cuts in parts of the country.

In a post on US social media platform X, the humanitarian group said it was “devastated and outraged” by the deaths, calling the incident “a direct attack on MSF.” It said 17 of its colleagues have been killed in Gaza. It said its health centers were clearly identifiable by its logo and that it shared their coordinates with the Israeli military, which was aware of them. “We express our solidarity with the families and loved ones of our colleagues,” said the group, adding that “Israeli authorities must be held accountable.” […]
